title: Branch prediction (hardware)
summary: Branch prediction predicts the outcome of conditional branches to keep the pipeline full. Static prediction: always taken/not-taken, backward taken/forward not-taken. Dynamic prediction: 1-bit (last outcome), 2-bit saturating counter (strongly/weakly taken/not-taken), gshare (global history XOR PC), tournament (local + global), TAGE (tagged geometric history length). Branch target buffer (BTB) caches branch targets. Return address stack (RAS) predicts return addresses.

structure.meaning: Predicts the same as the last outcome. Fails on alternating patterns.
States: 00 (strongly not-taken), 01 (weakly not-taken), 10 (weakly taken), 11 (strongly taken). Increment on taken, decrement on not-taken.
XOR global branch history with PC to index the prediction table. Captures correlations between branches.
Tagged Geometric History Length: multiple prediction tables with increasing history lengths. Uses partial tags for confidence.
Branch Target Buffer: caches the target address of branches. On a hit, the pipeline redirects to the target.
Return Address Stack: pushes return address on CALL, pops on RET. Predicts return targets.
Cost of a mispredicted branch: flush the pipeline and restart from the correct path.

notes: Branch prediction is critical for out-of-order and deeply pipelined CPUs.
TAGE (used by AMD/Intel) is one of the most accurate predictors.
Branch misprediction is a major source of performance loss in branchy code.
Speculative execution (based on prediction) can leak data via side channels (Spectre).
